fixes.explanation: I get it, friend. Courage is what you'd expect somebody to be missing. But the verse says something else. The father notices “…a young man lacking judgment…” (Proverbs 7:7). So the word is judgment, not courage.

Look at the verse again, friend. She says, “…I came out to meet you; I sought you, and I have found you.” (Proverbs 7:15). Those are her own words to him. So she does say she sought him and found him.

Exactly, friend. She says her husband “…took with him a bag of money and will not return till the moon is full.” (Proverbs 7:20). That's the timing she gives. She also says he's on a long journey (Proverbs 7:19), and she's telling this to the young man at twilight (Proverbs 7:9).

That's not the timing she gives, friend. She says her husband “…took with him a bag of money and will not return till the moon is full.” (Proverbs 7:20). She names the full moon, not a day of the week. The bag of money is in there too, so the trip sounds big.

Money does come up in her speech, friend, because she says her husband took a bag of money (Proverbs 7:20). But that's not how the verse says she gets the young man to follow her. It says, “With her great persuasion she entices him; with her flattering lips she lures him.” (Proverbs 7:21). So the word is lips.

That's right, friend. The father says, “Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her paths.” (Proverbs 7:25). He talks about the heart and about the paths in the same breath. I think that's worth hanging onto.
The father says much more than that, friend. He says, “For she has brought many down to death; her slain are many in number.” (Proverbs 7:26). So the number is many, not a few. It's a heavy line.
That's right, friend. The father says, “For she has brought many down to death; her slain are many in number.” (Proverbs 7:26). He says it in two ways, many and many in number. It's a heavy line.

It may look inviting at the door, friend, but that's not where the father says it leads. He says, “Her house is the road to Sheol, descending to the chambers of death.” (Proverbs 7:27). The road ends at the chambers of death, not at a feast. It's a sober way to finish.
